title: Kent After the Lamps
hook: Ordinary dark on a Kent curb. The rules do not get optional.
scene: You sit at a curb on a Kent residential that has gone overcast-night, not the Dark Hours yet, just the ordinary dark the Grid always had. Signals still cycle. A stale green somewhere to the west paints the wet. Ali in the glass: braid, wire rims, the pink hoodie gone gray in this light. The clipboard in the well has hours on it now. School zones. Stops. Turns. Bikes. A bus you may have passed. Space. Ice. A mill you refused to join. The Quiet uses the same paint at night. The rules do not get optional when the color drains. Tomorrow is more of this, then it is not — then it is someone else's act.
debrief: Night in The Grid is still The Grid. Lights work. Search harder. The Dark Hours are a later zone. Do not import highway night rules onto these two-lane stops just because the sky went out.

source.teaching_target: Night does not suspend residential rules; Act II remains search, space, and communication until the zone is clean.

image_brief.subject: Ali in profile in the cab at night, seen in the windshield glass: wire rims, cranberry braid the only warm color, faded hoodie gone gray in this light
image_brief.foreground: welded windshield mesh as a grid; a faint reflection of analog gauges in the glass; cracked dash gone almost brown
image_brief.midground: she sits at a Kent curb, looking out; a stale green from a distant cycling signal catches the rims
image_brief.background: ordinary overcast-night residential, wet empty street, one out-of-focus signal, no other cars, not the Dark Hours
image_brief.read: Ali is in the glass at a night curb — mesh, stale green, the hoodie no longer pink
